newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post page one Oct 10.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post page one Oct 10.

text.p: The Washington Post carried the following stories on its front page on Oct 10:

WASHINGTON - Two Americans and a Briton have won the Nobel Prize in chemistry for their discovery of a spherical form of carbon that wasn't supposed to exist and three Americans were awarded the Nobel Prize in physics for revealing that a form of helium can become a friction-free superfluid at extremely low temperatures.
WASHINGTON - Both the press and the public are using every available measure to tune out the contest between President Clinton and Bob Dole.

WASHINGTON - Hapless crack customers who came to Langley Park last weekend encountered dealers they had never seen before in a double-barrelled sting at the busiest and most flagrant open-air drug market in the Washington area.
WASHINGTON - The federal government is expected to finish the 1996 fiscal year with a budget deficit of $109 billion, according to a Congressional Budget Office estimate.

WASHINGTON - An increasingly nasty Virginia Senate race took a bizarre turn as Sen. John Warner's campaign acknowledged that its new ad casting his Democratic challenger as a liberal political insider contains an altered picture.
